sections.h2: Who sets and who collects the tax
sections.html:
Two offices split the work. The State Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT) decides what the property is worth. The county's Department of Finance sends the bill and takes the payment. Each level of government sets its own rate, so one bill can carry county, state and other charges.

OfficeRoleContact
SDAT Montgomery County Assessment OfficeValues, notices, appeals30 W. Gude Drive, Suite 400, Rockville; (240) 314-4510
County Department of FinanceBilling and collection, tax lien sale101 Monroe Street, 15th Floor, Rockville; 240-777-8860
MC311Tax questions(240) 777-0311

Expect the bill in July or August, covering the fiscal year that begins July 1. Finance also offers a tax credit for residents 65 and older and for retired military service members, plus an online portal to view or pay real property bills.

The county's general property tax rate was 1.0392 in both FY 2025 and FY 2026. It was 0.9905 in FY 2022, 0.9915 in FY 2023 and 1.0402 in FY 2024. These rates apply to assessed value, and the full bill also carries state and other charges. Special rates cover services the general rate does not fund, so a given street can pay more or less than the headline number.

The rate held flat for the year starting July 1, 2026, and yet plenty of homeowners saw a bigger bill. The next section explains why.

sections.h2: Why a bill can rise when the rate does not
sections.html:
Two changes pushed bills up in 2026: rising assessments and the end of a county credit. The Income Tax Offset Credit, shown on bills as the County Property Tax Credit, was $692 in levy year 2025. The County Council set it to $0 for 2026. It was not permanently repealed, and it only ever applied to owner-occupied principal residences.

Average homeowners faced about $23 more per month from higher assessments. If the council sets the credit above zero again, a homeowner needs a homestead application on file with SDAT by May 1, 2027 for it to appear on July 1, 2027 bills.

Because the council sets the credit anew each year, last year's bill says little about what a buyer will owe. Hand over the current bill instead.

sections.h2: The assessment cycle and the homestead cap
sections.html:
SDAT reappraises every property once every three years, so about one-third of Montgomery County homes get a new value each year. If the market value on the notice looks wrong to you, appeal it. Filing with SDAT is always free.

On a principal residence, the taxable assessment can climb at most 10% a year, or 5% in the Town of Kensington. Only owner-occupied principal residences get the homestead credit, and each county or town picks its own percentage from 0% to 10%. The 10% cap costs the county an estimated 0.4% of its assessable base in the fiscal 2026 table.

A purchase resets things: the cap is not applied in the first year, so an owner of many years and a new neighbor can be taxed on different figures. Your buyer's first bill may therefore look different from yours.

An appeal of a reassessment must be filed within 45 days of the date on the SDAT notice. The process has three levels, and the Appeals Board charges nothing.

  1. The Supervisor's level, an informal hearing with an assessor that usually lasts about 15 minutes. SDAT supplies a property worksheet and area sales listing beforehand.
  2. The Property Tax Assessment Appeals Board, with one board in each of the 24 jurisdictions, appointed by the Governor and independent of SDAT. Your request is due 30 days after the Supervisor's final notice.
  3. The Maryland Tax Court, which hears the case fresh and requires an in-person appearance. You have 30 days after the Board's order.

Buyers get a separate 60 day appeal window from the transfer date, though only when the sale falls after January 1 and before July 1 and the deed is already in the land records. If you close in that stretch, mention the option to your buyer.

A principal residence can be paid in two installments, September 30 and December 31. Anyone else follows the annual schedule: due July 1 without interest, overdue after October 1.

Splitting the payment can cost extra, since a local government may add up to 1.65% of the second installment as a service charge. Fees on the same bill, such as water and sewer, may be due with the first installment.

Ask about two relief programs. The state's Homeowners' Property Tax Credit depends on income and requires a fresh application each year; SDAT can give you the current deadline. The county senior credit equals 50% of the combined state credit and county supplement for residents 65 and older, and it also requires the state application.

The county turns unpaid taxes into a lien and sells it at an annual sealed-bid sale in June. To keep a property out of the sale, pay everything owed, with interest and penalties, no later than the last business day before it.

You still own the house after the sale, and you may redeem the lien until a Circuit Court order ends that right. Redemption interest on the certificate is 6% a year for owner-occupied properties and 20% a year for non-owner-occupied ones. A purchaser can seek foreclosure after 6 months, or 9 months for owner-occupied homes.

For scale, in the 2024 sales the county advertised 2,092 properties in the first notice, offered 1,327 for sale and sold 1,029 liens, and 1,184 were redeemed before foreclosure in FY 2024. The state also runs a Homeowner Protection Program and a Tax Sale Ombudsman, reachable at (410) 767-4994, for limited-income, elderly and disabled homeowners.

Back taxes are a lien, and the lien must be cleared for the title to pass cleanly. Ask the Department of Finance for a payoff, since penalties and interest continue until the balance is paid.

Closing also brings recordation and transfer tax, which the county reshaped in 2023. The guide to Montgomery County land records covers those charges. Deferred taxes under the optional program for owners 65 and older become a lien and are repaid when the property is transferred.

With a cash buyer, no lender is waiting in the background, and the payoff is taken out of the price at closing. Bring the current bill and your payoff letter to the title company so nothing is missed.

faqs.q: Who do I call about a Montgomery County property tax bill?
faqs.a: Start with MC311 at (240) 777-0311 or the Department of Finance at 240-777-8860. Questions about a value or appeal go to the SDAT Montgomery County assessment office at (240) 314-4510.

faqs.q: How long do I have to appeal a Montgomery County assessment?
faqs.a: Forty-five days from the SDAT notice date. Someone who bought from January 1 up to July 1 gets 60 days from the transfer, as soon as the deed is recorded.

faqs.q: When are Montgomery County property taxes due?
faqs.a: A principal residence can split the bill into September 30 and December 31 payments, and the second can include a service charge of up to 1.65%.

faqs.q: Is there a cap on how fast my Montgomery County assessment can rise?
faqs.a: Yes, for a principal residence: 10% a year, or 5% in the Town of Kensington. A purchase resets it, so the first year after a sale is not capped.

faqs.q: What is the redemption interest after a Montgomery County tax lien sale?
faqs.a: It is 6% a year for owner-occupied properties and 20% a year for non-owner-occupied properties. Redemption stays possible until a court order forecloses it.
